newsitem.title: ZAIRE: Zaire PM appoints national salvation government.
newsitem.headline: Zaire PM appoints national salvation government.

text.p: Zaire's emergency rule prime minister General Likulia Bolongo announced a 28-member national salvation government on Friday, with top army generals in charge of the key defence and interior ministries.

Likulia told a news conference that army chief of staff General Mahele Lieko Bokungo was his new defence minister and that General Ilunga Shamanga, who is close to President Mobutu Sese Seko, was his new interior minister.
Kamanda wa Kamanda, a member of the Kinshasa team at negotiations with rebels who control half the sprawling Central African nation, remains foreign minister.
Both Mahele, who remains army chief of staff, and Kamanda are deputy prime ministers.
Ilunga, the new interior minister, was previously Mobutu's personal chief of staff. "We have given this ministry the mission of national reconciliation," Likulia said of Ilunga's new role.
He said that Mahele had the task of national defence and restructuring Zaire's ragged and notoriously ill-disciplined army and turning it into a force that protected individual rights and freedoms.

Zaire's army, repeatedly routed by rebels who took up arms in October vowing to topple Mobutu, has a reputation for looting and terrorising civilians unfortunate enough to find themselves in its path.
Mobutu, who has dominated Zaire since seizing power in 1965, declared a nationwide state of emergency on Tuesday and appointed Likulia prime minister on Wednesday.
In doing so, he shunted aside his arch-foe, veteran opposition leader Etienne Tshisekedi, who had been in the job for under a week.
Mobutu had prostate cancer surgery in Europe in August. He is now back in Kinshasa.
